rules.rationale: Source ESOL value prior: smiles_short carried positive solubility effect; small solutes hydrate favorably.
Source prior gave smiles_long the largest negative effect; large hydrophobic solutes desolvate poorly.
Ring role had the highest transfer weight; rigid ring systems reduced solubility in source data.
Rotatable-bond role maps to branching; modest flexibility limited entropic desolvation penalty in source.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers ESOL size, ring and branching effects to hydration ranking. May fail because aqueous solubility mixes crystal-lattice terms absent from pure hydration free energy, and source role confidences are only 0.22-0.41.

rules.rationale: N/O heteroatoms donate and accept hydrogen bonds, the dominant favorable term in hydration free energy.
Apolar hydrocarbons pay a cavity-formation cost with no compensating polar solvation.
Halogenation raises hydrophobicity and weakens water hydrogen bonding despite added polarizability.
Counter-hypothesis: reverses the weakly supported negative smiles_mid source prior; moderate size allows more polar groups.

skills.hypothesis: Hydration is driven by polar hydrogen-bonding capacity rather than molecular size, so it reverses the mid-length source penalty. Fails if the score rewards small apolar solutes or if hetero_high coverage (28 items) is unrepresentative.

lesson: Source ESOL effects are size- and ring-dominated with low confidence (0.16-0.41), while hydration free energy is mechanistically governed by polar hydrogen bonding; prefer the mechanism-first prior and keep semantic mass decaying so revealed target data can override it.
revision_summary: Kept a trimmed source-grounded skill using only the explicit smiles_length value priors plus the two highest-transfer-weight roles (ring, branch). Added a counter-hypothesis domain skill that reverses the smiles_mid penalty and centers heteroatom and halogen-free polarity. Both capped at four catalog-exact rules with decaying semantic mass; deployed the mechanistic hydration skill.
